version_note: Harness revision 3 (2026-09-17, both pi tasks): the agent phase runs as the image's unprivileged `node` user (task.toml `[agent].user`; the checkout is node-owned, node_modules and the interpreters stay root-owned, vite gets writable temp dirs, root's git accepts the checkout), and `tests/test.sh` rejects a submission that changed pi source or the build/test toolchain (configs, manifests, scripts; `scope_exit_code`, reason in `scope.log`) before running any suite, and removes vite's transient bundles first. Motivation: the task review of 2026-09-17 reproduced a grading bypass in which a root agent replaced `node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs` and obtained reward 1 with Base code; the toolchain check also closes the tracked-config path. New control `control-toolchain-config-injected` (expected 0). The pass-to-pass check now tolerates the pinned environmental failures in the candidate run as well as in the baseline (a known timing-dependent case in pi's own suite failed for root in the rebuilt image after passing at build time; it is not attributable to a candidate). Image rebuilt; matrix and CI rerun recorded below. 0.0.4 harness revision 2 (2026-09-17): the lifecycle suite no longer leaks the runner's VITEST* variables into the child pi it spawns (a real pi never carries them); grok rollout 5 skipped its exit hooks under that variable and lost two lifecycle cases to it while being otherwise complete. Cases, oracle and controls unchanged. 0.0.4 (2026-09-16): one sentence of the lifecycle section restated so the outcome is unmistakable without naming a mechanism (a SIGTERM/SIGINT delivered to pi, interactive or headless, must still end the process once its managed processes are stopped), after the third grok and the third opus rollout both left a headless pi running after SIGTERM with the 0.0.2/0.0.3 wording; and verifier harness revision: the between-test drain waits 300 ms and for an idle session, and a verifier prompt waits for an idle session first, because the contract lets a wake start a turn at any idle moment and an implementation may report an exit a little after the process died (the opus 0.0.3 submission lost four cases to that spill-over, none of them a contract violation). Cases, oracle and controls unchanged. 0.0.3 (2026-09-16) rewrites the same requirements in the voice of an issue (where it comes from, what we are asking for, the interface we agreed on, what we expect to see, the lifecycle that bit us before) instead of a specification; every tool, parameter, result shape, rule and lifecycle expectation of 0.0.2 is kept verbatim or near-verbatim, and no mechanism hint was added. Verifier, oracle and controls unchanged. 0.0.2 (2026-09-16) rewrites the instruction to state outcomes and the tool/message contract only: the mechanism hints of 0.0.1 are gone (own process group and detached stdio, overriding the built-in tool by name, pi.sendMessage, pi's steering delivery, re-raising the signal, SessionManager.getSessionDir() and per-pi-process keying, writing logs as they arrive, the built-in bash truncation limits and error strings). Verifier, oracle and controls are unchanged, so the 0.0.1 Harbor matrix and the four real rollouts (all on the 0.0.1 wording) carry over; new rollouts on the 0.0.2 wording are still to be run.
